overview.description: Carpet is a simple and rewarding patience (solitaire) game. Four Aces form the foundations, twenty cards are laid out in a 5Ã—4 grid called the 'carpet,' and the remaining cards form a stock. The goal is to build all cards onto the foundations in suit from Ace to King.

history.origins: Carpet is a traditional patience game of unknown origin. It belongs to the 'Calculation' family of solitaire games. The name comes from the 5Ã—4 grid of cards resembling a carpet pattern.
timeline: Traditional origins: Unknown date, likely 19th or early 20th century
Modern: Included in solitaire software collections
Current: Popular as an easy-to-win patience game
history.evolution: The game has remained relatively unchanged. Digital versions have made it more accessible and often include autoplay features for obvious moves.
history.cultural: Known as a relaxing, simple builder game. Most games are winnable with careful play, making it popular for casual solitaire play.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card pack. Remove the four Aces to form foundations. The remaining 48 cards are shuffled.
setup.equipment: Standard deck of cards, playing surface
setup.dealing: Remove four Aces and place them as foundations. Deal 20 cards face up in a 5Ã—4 grid (the 'carpet') with no overlaps. Remaining 28 cards form the stock (held in hand). Discard pile starts empty.

rules.objective: Move all cards onto the four foundations, building each up in suit from Ace to King.
rules.gameplay: Foundations build up in suit (Aceâ†’2â†’3â†’...â†’King). Cards available for play: all cards in the carpet, and the top card of the discard pile. Empty spaces in the carpet may be filled from the discard pile. Deal from stock one card at a time onto discard pile at any time. No redeals - when stock is empty, dealing stops.
keyRules: Remove four Aces to start foundations
Foundations build up in suit to King
Carpet cards and top discard available for play
Empty carpet spaces filled from discard pile
Deal one card at a time from stock

strategy.basic: Always play to foundations as soon as possible - there's no reason to delay. This is the primary rule of Carpet.
strategy.intermediate: Use empty carpet spaces strategically to hold dealt cards you can play soon. Try to create chains of same-suit cards in the carpet so they can cascade to foundations.
strategy.advanced: Plan several moves ahead. Create same-suit sequences in the carpet (e.g., 4-5-6-7-8 of Spades) so when the 4 goes to foundation, the rest follow quickly. Keep high cards in discard until foundations are built up close to their level, or until you have free carpet space.

Use carpet spaces for cards you can play soon
Create same-suit chains in the carpet for cascading plays
Keep high cards in discard until foundations are ready
Fill empty carpet spaces from discard strategically

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.
